Class AbstractPanelElement

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.AbstractPanelElement
All Implemented Interfaces:
PanelElement
Direct Known Subclasses:
Button, Checkbox, Divider, Dropdown, DropdownMulti, Flow, Icon, InfoBox, ItemDisplay, ProgressBar, Radio, ScrollContainer, Section, Slider, SlotElement, SlotFlowElement, Tabs, TextField, TextLabel, Toggle
public abstract class AbstractPanelElement extends Object implements PanelElement
Base of MenuKit's own elements: built once by a builder, immutable after (§0066, applying §0022 to elements).

One vocabulary

Every element's builder extends AbstractPanelElement.Builder, so the same idea has the same name on every element:
  • at(x, y): position in the panel's content area.
  • size(w, h): on the elements that take a size (the rest size themselves from their content).
  • visibleWhen(supplier): shown while it holds, read every frame.
  • disabledWhen(supplier): greyed and inert while it holds.
  • tooltip(text): the hover tooltip.
  • state(get, set): the lens onto the consumer's value, on every element that shows one (§0026). An element never stores the value: it reads get every frame and hands a change to set.
  • onClick(Runnable): what a press does.
  • style(ControlStyle): MenuKit's look or vanilla's.
  • opaque(boolean): whether it is solid on a transparent panel.
  • declId(id): a stable id for the window's address.

What an instance keeps

Only what a container needs: setChildPosition(int, int) (a Flow or a Row/Column places its children), and the layout protocol a panel drives every pass (layoutWithin(int), fillWidth(int)). Nothing else about an element changes after build(); what varies at runtime is read from suppliers.

The one width-cap helper

An element given a size keeps its authored width as its naturalWidth(); the panel's layout pass caps the live width to the room it has (min(authored, budget)), reversibly, and a column's CrossAlign.FILL re-authors it (fillWidth(int)). Elements that size themselves from content, or never shrink (an icon, a checkbox square), override these.

Disabled

disabled(RenderContext) and disabled(InputContext) answer "should this element look and act disabled now": its own disabledWhen, or the disabled panel or container around it (the cascade the contexts carry).

Consumer custom elements

A consumer may extend this class for its own element, with its own builder extending AbstractPanelElement.Builder (and the protected constructor taking it), or with the no-argument constructor and its own fields; or implement PanelElement directly.

    • setChildPosition

      public void setChildPosition(int x, int y)
      Moves this element (the container protocol): a Flow places its children with it every layout pass, and Row/Column place a built element with it. Render and input read the position every frame, so a move takes effect on the next frame. Client-side presentation only; the element's identity is unchanged.
